question_text:
An annual squash tournament groups players into 5 divisions according to their skill level.
The table shows the number of players at the tournament over 3 years.
Find the probability that a player:

subparts.stem: in the 2017 tournament played in division 1

mark_breakdown.desc: Setting up the ratio of division 1 players in 2017 to total 2017 players

subparts.solution: $\text{P}(\text{player in the 2017 tournament played in division 1}) \approx \frac{4}{61} \approx 0.0656$.

ai_explanation.concept_rule: Probability of an event within a restricted condition is given by $\frac{\text{favourable outcomes}}{\text{total outcomes for that group}}$.
step_by_step: Look at the column for 2017: total players = 61.
ai_explanation.common_pitfalls: Dividing by the overall total (169) instead of the 2017 total (61).

subparts.stem: in any of the past tournaments played in division 3

mark_breakdown.desc: Summing division 3 players across all years and total players across all years

subparts.solution: There were $13 + 12 + 14 = 39$ division 3 players in total, and $61 + 51 + 57 = 169$ players in total. $\therefore \text{P}(\text{player in any of the past tournaments played in division 3}) \approx \frac{39}{169} \approx 0.231$.

ai_explanation.concept_rule: For a selection across all past tournaments, use the overall totals across all columns.
step_by_step: Sum the total number of players: $61 + 51 + 57 = 169$.
ai_explanation.common_pitfalls: Using the total from only one year instead of the sum of all years.

subparts.stem: in the 2019 tournament did not play in division 2 or 4.

mark_breakdown.desc: Finding the number of 2019 players not in division 2 or 4

subparts.solution: In the 2019 tournament, 8 players played in division 2 and 14 players played in division 4. So, $57 - 8 - 14 = 35$ players in the 2019 tournament did not play in division 2 or 4. $\therefore \text{P}(\text{player in the 2019 tournament did not play in division 2 or 4}) \approx \frac{35}{57} \approx 0.614$.

ai_explanation.concept_rule: Use the complement rule: subtract the unwanted categories from the total for that column.
step_by_step: Consider the 2019 tournament with total 57 players.
Identify division 2 players (8) and division 4 players (14).
Subtract to find those not in division 2 or 4: $57 - (8 + 14) = 35$ (or sum divisions 1, 3, 5: $5 + 14 + 16 = 35$).
ai_explanation.common_pitfalls: Adding division 2 and 4 players instead of excluding them.
